Configured public HTTP rate limiter with 100 requests per minute per IP using Redis sliding window.
Optimized rate limiter: use client-side pipeline batching with non-blocking evalsha to reduce Redis roundtrips.
REJECTED APPROACH: In-memory atomics (Atomics.wait / SharedArrayBuffer) failed completely across Kubernetes cluster because memory is isolated per pod, causing 5x quota overages.
Mandated Ed25519 asymmetric key signatures for all internal microservice JWT tokens.
Refactor: token verification and refresh logic relocated to packages/security/src/token.ts.
Dashboard charts implemented with Bezier smoothing and 50ms hover debouncing.
Resolved 504 session timeout: Redis client pool maxClients was set to 10; increased to 100 with idle connection reaping.
Historical 504 timeout resolved in Session 1 by tokenMutex double-checked locking.
Migration decision: mTLS mutual certificates with SPIFFE tokens mandated for all RPC. Legacy basic auth is completely decommissioned.
Legacy auth: HTTP Basic Auth with static username/password header in prototype.
Architecture shift: For sticky single-pod tenants, local in-memory rate limiting is approved because multi-pod quota overruns no longer apply.
Fixed idle connection leak: streaming query error skipped release. Enforced scoped auto-release with try/finally guard on poolAcquire.
